title: Response Adequacy and Pattern-of-Failure Figures in Employer Benefit Charging
content:
Employer Benefit Charging measures an employer's record of answering notices of claim with two figures that must both be met to form a pattern of failure: a count and a rate, taken over a lookback period. The figures are the same in all seven charge classes.

| Charge class | Untimely or inadequate responses (count) | Share of notices answered untimely or inadequately (rate) | Lookback (calendar days before the overpayment determination) | Adequate response means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Separating Employer — Most Recent | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Base Period Employer — Proportional Share | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Continuing Part-Time Base Period Employer | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Combined Wage Claim Contributing Employer | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Extended Benefits State-Share Employer | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Reimbursing Nonprofit Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |
| Reimbursing Governmental Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar | 2 | 0.02 (2%) | 365 | Separation reason, dates and wages all answered |

## How the measure is taken

The measure looks at the employer account's positions whose notice of claim was mailed within the 365 calendar days before the overpayment determination date. It counts those positions whose response timeliness is late or none (no response), and it also divides that count by all positions noticed in the same period. A response is adequate only when the separation reason, the dates and the wages are all answered.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

| Positions noticed in the lookback | Late or unanswered among them | Count test (at least 2) | Rate test (at least 2%) | Pattern of failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 2 | Met | Met (4%) | Yes |
| 50 | 1 | Not met | Met (2%) | No |
| 120 | 2 | Met | Not met (about 1.7%) | No |
| 100 | 2 | Met | Met (exactly 2%) | Yes |

Both tests must be met; meeting only one of them does not form a pattern of failure.
